description: The cursor rules of POST /api/station/events as golden sequences (contracts/README.md, Events). tests/test_contracts_events_cursor.py replays each against a real hub over HTTP, on a hub that has never had a post. `events`: the made-up events the sequences use, by name ({type, data}; `item`: that JSON value itself in place of an event; `hub_fails`: the test makes the hub fail to apply it for a reason of the hub's own). A step is a post and what must follow: `post.events` is a list of [seq, event name] (seq null: the event is sent without one; an event is sent as {seq, at, type, data, audio: null, audio_dropped: false}), `status` the HTTP status, `answer` the keys of the 200 answer, `cursor` the hub's [epoch, seq] afterwards, `applied_times` how many times each named `activity` event has been applied on the hub so far (an activity adds to its minute's count, so twice shows; the test replays the events' minutes as minutes of half an hour ago, since a hub drops old activity when it starts), `errors` the hub's count of events it failed to apply so far. `{restart: true}`: the hub is stopped and started again on the same database. `from_762` on a step: what that step answers once #762 is on main (the keys it gives replace the step's own); `rule_from_762`: the sequence's rule from then on. The test replays those instead when its E1 switch is flipped. The other sequences are the same before and after.

sequences.name: in-order
sequences.rule: Events are applied in `seq` order and the answer's `acked` is the highest `seq` dealt with.

sequences.name: a-retry-is-skipped
sequences.rule: A post delivered before (the station got no answer and sent it again) is skipped whole: `seq` at or under the cursor is never applied twice.

sequences.name: an-overlap-applies-the-new-ones
sequences.rule: A post that overlaps the cursor: what is at or under it is skipped, the rest applied.

sequences.name: a-seq-used-twice-is-lost
sequences.rule: `seq` is never used twice within an epoch: a second event under a `seq` the hub has dealt with is skipped as delivered before, and acked. The station then deletes it.

sequences.name: sorted-within-a-post
sequences.rule: The hub sorts a post's events by `seq` before it applies them.

sequences.name: a-gap-is-not-noticed
sequences.rule: The hub does not check that `seq` is the cursor plus one: it applies an event past a gap and moves the cursor to it. What comes later with a `seq` inside the gap is skipped, and acked.

sequences.name: a-new-epoch-restarts
sequences.rule: A post with another epoch than the last one's sets the cursor to 0: everything in it is applied, from `seq` 1.

sequences.name: the-cursor-survives-a-hub-restart
sequences.rule: The cursor is kept in the hub's database once per post: a retry after the hub restarted is still skipped.

sequences.name: an-empty-post-reads-the-cursor
sequences.rule: A post with no events answers the cursor of its epoch and applies nothing. (It still switches the epoch: with another epoch it answers 0 and the hub's cursor is then that epoch's.)

sequences.name: one-cursor-for-every-sender
sequences.rule: KNOWN DEVIATION E3. The hub has one cursor, not one per station or per epoch: a post from another outbox moves it, and a retry from the first outbox is then taken as new and applied a second time.

sequences.name: a-post-without-an-epoch-moves-the-cursor
sequences.rule: A post without `epoch` is taken as epoch "": it moves the cursor like any other epoch.

sequences.name: an-event-that-fails-is-acked-and-skipped
sequences.rule: KNOWN DEVIATION E1. An event the hub fails to apply (here: a clip id it refuses) is counted, logged, skipped and ACKED: the answer covers it and has no word about it, so the station deletes it. The events behind it are applied.
sequences.rule_from_762: E1 as #762 fixes it: the event is still skipped and the cursor still moves past it, but the answer lists it under `rejected` with why (`malformed`: it can never apply, here a clip id the hub refuses; `apply_failed`: the hub's own trouble), and the station keeps it aside.

sequences.name: an-unknown-type-is-acked
sequences.rule: An event of a type the hub does not know is logged and acked; nothing is applied, it is no error, and it counts in `applied`.

sequences.name: what-is-skipped-without-a-word
sequences.rule: An item of `events` that is not an object is skipped. An event without `seq` is taken as `seq` 0: at or under every cursor, so never applied, and no error.
sequences.rule_from_762: From #762 on an event needs a `seq` that is an integer from 1: an item that is not an object and an event without one are listed under `rejected` as `malformed`, by their index in the post (`seq` null), never applied, and never move the cursor.

rejected.error: an event needs a seq (an integer from 1)
an event needs a seq (an integer from 1)

sequences.name: a-source-event-the-hub-fails-is-sent-again
sequences.rule: The one exception to E1: a `source_event` the hub fails to apply for a reason of its own (not a malformed one) is NOT acked, and nothing behind it in the post is looked at: `acked` stays under it and the station sends it again. On its third delivery it is given up like any other event.
sequences.rule_from_762: As before for its first two deliveries (not acked, nothing behind it looked at, no `rejected`); on the third it is given up, acked, and listed under `rejected` as `apply_failed`: the station keeps it aside and sends it again later, as a new event.

sequences.name: a-malformed-source-event-is-acked-and-skipped
sequences.rule: A `source_event` that is not one (its `event` breaks the interface) is skipped and acked like any other failed event; a good one is applied.
sequences.rule_from_762: The same, and from #762 on it is listed under `rejected` as `malformed` (its error is the type only: a feed's text never leaves the hub's log).

sequences.name: seq-as-a-string-or-a-float
sequences.rule: The hub reads `seq` with int(): a string of digits and a float are taken (the float cut to its whole part). A writer sends an integer.
sequences.rule_from_762: From #762 on the hub takes neither: a `seq` that is a string or a float is `malformed`, listed by its index, not applied, and the cursor stays.

rejected.error: an event needs a seq (an integer from 1)
an event needs a seq (an integer from 1)

sequences.name: a-seq-that-is-no-number-refuses-the-whole-post
sequences.rule: A `seq` that int() does not take is 400 for the whole post: nothing of it is applied and the cursor stays. The station sends the same post again (KNOWN DEVIATION E2).
sequences.rule_from_762: From #762 on it no longer refuses the post: that one event is `malformed`, listed by its index, and the rest of the post is applied.

rejected.error: an event needs a seq (an integer from 1)

sequences.name: a-body-that-is-no-events-post
sequences.rule: A body that is not an object with an `events` list is 400; a `station` that is another id than the token's is 401 `id_mismatch`. The cursor stays.
sequences.rule_from_762: The same, and from #762 on the 400 says why in `reason`: `bad_batch` (`bad_json` for a body that is not JSON; a 413 says `too_large` and `max_bytes`).
